mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY growth is below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that falls below 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained INDPRO declines > -0.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) where both decline simultaneously by more than 1% month-over-month signals a synchronized contraction in major demand components, which increases recession risk and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > -1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline > -1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) both rise simultaneously by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise > +0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 per month for four consecutive months, combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals robust labor market expansion without wage inflation, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 for four consecutive months AND UNRATE stable (change < 0.1pp)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS > 200,000 for four months and UNRATE is stable.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between real retail sales (RSAFS) growth and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days; higher-than-expected monthly RSAFS growth signals near-term consumer confidence and boosts earnings expectations, leading to positive returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS growth exceeds consensus forecast by more than 0.5%.
